name: Analogical Prompting
executive_summary: Ask the model to generate its own relevant worked examples before solving the actual problem, removing the need for a hand-labeled exemplar set entirely.
description: Instead of supplying few-shot exemplars, the prompt asks the model to first recall or invent problems related to the target and solve those, then use that self-generated context to solve the real problem — an analogy to how a human might recall a similar solved problem before tackling a new one.
when_to_use: No hand-labeled few-shot exemplars are available and writing them is costly.
when_not_to_use: High-quality curated exemplars already exist — hand-picked or actively-selected exemplars generally outperform self-generated ones.
known_pitfalls: Self-generated 'similar problems' can be superficially similar but structurally misleading, propagating a bad analogy into a bad solution.

primary_source.authors: Yasunaga, Chen, Li, Pásztor, Leskovec, Liang, Zhou
primary_source.title: Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners

usage_templates.template:
Problem: {{problem}}

# Step 1: Recall
Recall {{num_related}} distinct problems that are related to this one and briefly explain why each is related.

# Step 2: Solve the related problems
Solve each of the {{num_related}} related problems, showing your reasoning.

# Step 3: Solve the target
Using the related problems and their solutions above as guidance, now solve the original problem: {{problem}}

variables.name: num_related
variables.description: How many self-generated analogous problems to produce

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
